successors.name: Painted Grey Ware culture
successors.text: the Ochre Coloured Pottery culture was succeeded by the Painted Grey Ware culture (infobox 'followed by: Black and red ware, Painted Grey Ware culture')

ledger.x: c. 2000 BCE: the Ochre Coloured Pottery culture appears in north-eastern Rajasthan and along the Sahibi river. Infobox 'c. 2000-1500 BCE'; 'Early characteristic ceramics near Jodhpura (Jaipur district, Rajasthan) date to the 3rd millennium'; sites lie 'along the Sahibi River and its tributaries, the Krishnavati and…

c. 1900 BCE: the culture reaches the Gangetic plain. The page says only 'the early 2nd millennium BCE' for this and Uesugi's c. 1900-1300 BCE for the culture; -1900 is my bridging year. The Copper Hoard page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copper_Hoard_culture) puts the hoards 'mainly in the western Ganges-Yamuna doab'…
c. 1500 BCE: the Ochre Coloured Pottery culture ends and gives way to the Painted Grey Ware culture. Infobox 'c. 2000-1500 BCE'; the page says it was succeeded by Painted Grey Ware.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture known from villages and copper hoards ('most sites are small, densely distributed villages'), not from frontiers.
